entries.title: environment variables stay supported, and no longer warn that 2.0 removes them
entries.summary: The config loader no longer logs "Deprecated: ... will be removed in v2.0" when a `JCODEMUNCH_*` variable fills a key the config file leaves unset, and CONFIGURATION.md documents env vars as a supported fallback (a config file value still wins). No 2.0 is planned. `JCODEMUNCH_SHARE_SAVINGS=0`, the documented opt-out from anonymous savings sharing, keeps working. A test fails if a loader message or a tracked doc promises a 2.0 removal again.

entries.title: git blame is off by default, and it no longer adds "2 properties" to a file summary
entries.summary: Indexing no longer runs a timed `git log` on every git repository by default: `git_blame_enabled` defaults to `false`, and an existing config that sets the key keeps its value. With it on, the provider runs as before minus the "2 properties" suffix it added to every file summary it covered. SECURITY.md now lists it, since it stores commit authors' names in the index and, with AI summaries on, sends them to the summarizer. Search ranking doesn't move.

entries.title: SQL procedures, triggers and constraints are indexed, and one unparseable statement no longer loses the rest of the file
entries.summary: T-SQL and Sybase stored procedures and triggers are symbols, a bracket-quoted name reads as `schema.name`, and tables, views and indexes have their own kinds (#1080, @outoftheblue9). A SQL script is parsed one batch at a time, so a statement the grammar cannot parse costs only its own batch, and named constraints are symbols (#1081, @outoftheblue9). Search ranking no longer depends on whether git blame finished inside its time budget, or on today's date. Existing indexes are re-parsed once.

entries.title: init writes hooks that run the install you ran, not the first one on PATH
entries.summary: `init` wrote every hook, the Codex server entry and the post-upgrade hook refresh with the first `jcodemunch-mcp` on PATH, so running a newer install's `init` from a venv or a `uv tool` environment, with an older install on PATH, gave hooks that call the older version. They now name the install that ran. Under `uvx`, whose cache `uv cache clean` deletes, `init` writes the next install on PATH and prints which, with the command that makes the hooks call the version you ran.
